texts.full_text: tor, Joyce Bonzey. At issue is Bonzey's claimed exemption of a 1992 pontiac automobile which was purchased with proceeds traceable to her workers' compensation benefits. The Debtor contends that R.I.Gen.Laws § 28-33-27 authorizes such an exemption, while the Trustee argues that the exemption ended when Bonzey received a lump sum compensation payment for her work-related injury. FACTS In 1990 Joyce Bonzey sustained a back injury at work, and said injury was determined to be compensable under Rhode Island workers' compensation law. In September 1992, her injury claim was settled and the Workers' Compensation Commission approved a $46,000 lump sum payment to compensate Bonzey for her injury and to cover her workers' compensation claim. Bonzey used a portion of the lump sum payment to purchase a 1992 Pontiac automobile, and the purchase of the automobile was the subject of the claim of exemption. Bonzey claimed the automobile was exempt from the bankruptcy estate under the exemption provisions of the Rhode Island workers' compensation statute, R.I. Gen.
